items.title: Section: Six Ways of Dwelling Close All Thirteen Ascetic Practices

items.zh: 謂住空閑山林坰野，受用邊際所有臥具，遠離一切村邑聚落。如是名為住阿練若。云何名為常居樹下？謂常期願住於樹下，依止樹根。如是名為常居樹下。云何名為常居逈露？謂常期願住於逈露，無覆障處。如是名為常居逈露。云何名為常住塚間？謂常期願住塚墓間，諸有命過送尸骸處。如是名為常住塚間。云何名為常期端坐？謂於大床、或小繩床、或草葉座端身而坐，推度時日，終不以背或以其脇，依倚大床、或小繩床、或壁、或樹、草葉座等。如是名為常期端坐。云何名為處如常座？謂所坐臥或諸草座、或諸葉座，如舊敷設草座、葉座而常坐臥，一敷設後，終不數數翻舉修理。
items.en: Dwelling in the forest means living in quiet forests and open wilderness, using only the most minimal bedding, far from every village or town. Dwelling constantly beneath a tree means resolving always to dwell at the root of a tree. Dwelling constantly in the open means resolving always to dwell in open, unsheltered places. Dwelling constantly near a charnel ground means resolving always to dwell where the dead are brought and their remains laid to rest. Always sitting upright means sitting properly on a bed, rope-bed, or grass seat, passing the days this way, never reclining against a bed, wall, tree, or seat with one's back or side. Remaining in one's fixed seat means that, once a grass or leaf seat has been laid out, one sits and lies there as it already stands, never repeatedly rearranging or refashioning it.

items.zh: 如是名為處如常座。問：何故名為杜多功德？

items.title: Section: Why "Ascetic Virtues" — The Carded Wool Analogy

items.zh: 答：譬如世間或毛或㲲，未鞭、未彈、未紛、未擘，爾時相著，不軟不輕，不任造作縷綫氈褥。若鞭、若彈、若紛、若擘，爾時分散，柔軟輕妙，堪任造作縷綫氈褥。如是行者，由飲食貪，於諸飲食令心染著；由衣服貪，於諸衣服令心染著；由敷具貪，於諸敷具令心染著。彼由如是杜多功德，能淨修治，令其純直，柔軟輕妙，有所堪任，隨順依止，能修梵行。是故名為杜多功德。
items.en: It is like wool or cotton fibre in the world: before it has been whipped, plucked, combed, or carded, it clings together, neither soft nor light, unfit to be made into thread, yarn, or felted cloth. Once whipped, plucked, combed, and carded, it comes apart, soft and light, fit to be made into thread, yarn, or felted cloth. In just the same way, a practitioner's mind clings, through craving for food, to food; through craving for clothing, to clothing; through craving for bedding, to bedding. Through these ascetic virtues, such a one is purified and refined, becoming genuinely simple and upright, soft, light, and capable — fit to rely upon in practising pure conduct. This is why they are called ascetic virtues.

items.title: Section: Each Practice Matched to the Specific Craving It Cuts

items.zh: 於飲食中，有美食貪及多食貪，能障修善。為欲斷除美食貪故，常期乞食、次第乞食。為欲斷除多食貪故，但一坐食、先止後食。於衣服中，有三種貪，能障修善。一、多衣貪，二、軟觸貪，三、上妙貪。為欲斷除多衣貪故，但持三衣。為欲斷除於諸衣服軟觸貪故，但持毳衣。為欲斷除於諸衣服上妙貪故，持糞掃衣。於諸敷具有四種貪，能障修善。一、諠雜貪，二、屋宇貪，三、倚樂臥樂貪，四、敷具貪。為欲斷除諠雜貪故，住阿練若。為欲斷除屋宇貪故，常居樹下、逈露、塚間。又為斷除婬佚貪故，常住塚間。
items.en: Regarding food, there is craving for delicious food and craving for eating too much, both obstructing wholesome cultivation. To cut off craving for delicious food, one practices regular and sequential begging. To cut off craving for eating too much, one eats only one sitting's worth and only before a fixed time. Regarding clothing, there are three cravings obstructing wholesome cultivation: craving for many robes, craving for soft texture, and craving for fine quality. To cut off craving for many robes, one keeps only three robes. To cut off craving for soft texture, one wears only coarse wool. To cut off craving for fine quality, one wears only discarded rags. Regarding bedding, there are four cravings obstructing wholesome cultivation: craving for lively company, craving for a proper dwelling, craving for the comfort of reclining and lying down, and craving for fine bedding itself. To cut off craving for lively company, one dwells in the forest. To cut off craving for a proper dwelling, one dwells constantly beneath a tree, in the open, or near a charnel ground. And to cut off craving rooted in lust specifically, one dwells constantly near a charnel ground.

items.title: Section: Ascetic Virtues Formally Close; Dignified Bearing and Proper Measure

items.zh: 為欲斷除倚樂臥樂貪故，常期端坐。為欲斷除敷具貪故，處如常座。是名成就杜多功德。云何端嚴？謂能成就若往、若還、若覩、若瞻、若屈、若伸、持僧伽胝持衣持鉢，端嚴形相。是名端嚴。云何知量？謂於淨信諸婆羅門、長者、居士，極恣衣服、飲食、敷具、病緣醫藥諸什物中，知量而聚。是名知量。
items.en: To cut off craving for the comfort of reclining and lying down, one always sits upright. To cut off craving for fine bedding itself, one remains in one's fixed seat. This is accomplishing the virtues of ascetic practice. What is dignified bearing? It is maintaining a dignified form in going and returning, looking and gazing, bending and stretching, and carrying the great robe, the robes, and the bowl. This is called dignified bearing. What is proper measure? It means that, when devout brahmins, elders, or householders offer clothing, food, bedding, medicine, or other necessities without any limit, one takes only what is appropriate. This is called proper measure.

items.title: The Qualities of a Good Person, and the Marks of a Wise One

items.zh: 云何成就賢善士法？謂生高族淨信出家，或生富族淨信出家，顏容殊妙，喜見端嚴，具足多聞，語具圓滿，或隨獲得少智、少見、少安樂住。由是因緣，不自高舉，不陵[＊]蔑他；能知唯有法隨法行，是其諦實。既了知已，精進修行法隨法行。是名成就賢善士法。云何成就聰慧者相？謂由作業相表知愚夫，由作業相表知聰慧。其事云何？謂諸愚夫，惡思所思、惡說所說、惡作所作；諸聰慧者，善思所思、善說所說、善作所作。是名成就聰慧者相。
items.en: What is accomplishing the qualities of a good person? It means one born into a noble family, or a wealthy one, who went forth with genuine faith; of fine appearance, pleasing to behold; possessed of extensive learning and complete, skilful speech; or one who has gained some small wisdom, some small insight, some small taste of peaceful abiding. Because of this, one does not become conceited or look down on others, but recognises that practising in accordance with the Dharma [the eightfold path that accords with nirvāṇa] is the one true and genuine task — and having understood this, diligently practices accordingly. This is accomplishing the qualities of a good person. What is accomplishing the marks of a wise person? Fools think unwholesome thoughts, speak unwholesome words, and perform unwholesome deeds; the wise think wholesome thoughts, speak wholesome words, and perform wholesome deeds. This is accomplishing the marks of a wise person.

items.title: Patience: Towards Hostility and Towards Genuine Hardship

items.zh: 云何堪忍？謂如有一，罵不報罵、瞋不報瞋、打不報打、弄不報弄。又彼尊者，堪能忍受寒熱、飢渴、蚊虻、風日、蛇蠍毒觸，又能忍受他所干犯、麁惡語言，又能忍受身中所有猛利、堅勁、辛楚、切心、奪命苦受。為性堪忍，有所容受。是名堪忍。
items.en: What is patience? It is like one who does not repay abuse with abuse, anger with anger, a blow with a blow, mockery with mockery. Such a venerable one is also able to bear cold and heat, hunger and thirst, mosquitoes and gnats, wind and sun, the poisonous bite of snakes and scorpions, and is able to bear others' transgressions and harsh speech, and is able to bear severe, sharp, agonising, life-threatening pain arising within the body itself. Being patient by nature, one has genuine capacity to endure. This is called patience.

blocks.text: The ascetic practices concerning dwelling, why they are called "dhūta", and further ornaments.
In the forest, far from villages; always beneath a tree; always in the open; always near a charnel ground; always sitting upright (never lying down); remaining in one's fixed seat.

"Like wool or cotton fibre: before it has been whipped, plucked, combed, and carded, it clings together, neither soft nor light, unfit to be made into thread. Once carded, it comes apart, soft and light." So the mind, shaken free of craving, becomes pliant.

Sequential begging cuts craving for delicious food; eating at one sitting cuts craving to eat too much; the three robes cut craving for many robes; living near a charnel ground cuts lust. Venerable Miào Jìng: one sees corpses and the mind turns away from desire.
Dignified bearing in every posture; knowing the proper measure. The qualities of a good person: faith, learning, skilful speech.

"Fools think unwholesome thoughts, speak unwholesome words, perform unwholesome deeds; the wise think, speak, and do what is wholesome." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Dharma" here is nirvāṇa; "conforming Dharma" is the eightfold path.
"Not repaying abuse with abuse", and bearing cold and heat, hunger and thirst, mosquitoes, wind and sun.

quiz.q: Why are they called ascetic virtues, what simile does the text use, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say they mainly counter?
options: wool whipped, plucked, combed, and carded becomes soft and usable; they mainly counter craving
quiz.why: "Once whipped, plucked, combed, and carded, it comes apart, soft and light, fit to be made into thread, yarn, or felted cloth." Master Cháng Bǎi: the function of the ascetic virtues is chiefly to counter craving; with craving one cannot cultivate the noble path.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain dwelling near a charnel ground to cut off lust?
options: the charnel ground is foul and impure, so lustful thoughts fade
quiz.why: "And to cut off craving rooted in lust specifically, one dwells constantly near a charnel ground." Venerable Miào Jìng: living by the charnel ground, all is foul and impure, so lustful thoughts disappear.

quiz.q: How does the treatise tell fools from the wise, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng say this shows?
options: fools think, speak, and act badly; the wise think, speak, and act well — no words needed, actions show it
quiz.why: "Fools think unwholesome thoughts, speak unwholesome words, and perform unwholesome deeds; the wise think wholesome thoughts, speak wholesome words, and perform wholesome deeds." Venerable Miào Jìng: you needn't tell anyone whether you are foolish or wise — your actions show it.

quiz.q: The English renders 法隨法行 as "practising the teaching in accordance with the teaching." How do the masters explain it?
options: Miào Jìng: Dharma is nirvāṇa, conforming Dharma the eightfold path; Cháng Bǎi adds Vasubandhu's reading — Dharma is the scriptures, conforming practice follows them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Dharma" here is nirvāṇa; "conforming Dharma" is the eightfold path, which is not nirvāṇa but accords with it. Master Cháng Bǎi: "Dharma" is all the scriptures, Vinaya, and treatises; "conforming" is practising by the methods they point to.
